mappings.note: The work is telling two simple permanent tissues apart from an observed property (coconut fibre vs coriander stalk = sclerenchyma vs collenchyma), so LO-1 leads; C-4.2-LO-2 carries the lignified-dead-wall-to-brittleness step. Not C-4.2-LO-3: nothing is asked about what either tissue does for the plant.

A single structural feature (waxy cuticle) is traded against two habitats, which is exactly structure-related-to-function, so C-4.2-LO-2 leads; C-4.2-LO-3 covers the protective role of the epidermis. Not LO-1 - only one tissue is in play, nothing is being differentiated.

The question is about the mechanism of water transport (transpiration pull, root to leaf), which C3.2 names outright as a life process; C-4.2-LO-3 covers the role of xylem. Chosen over C-4.2-LO-2 because the dead-cell structure is given in the stem, not asked for.

A remove-the-tissue-and-predict question, i.e. the role of stomata in the plant body, so C-4.2-LO-3 leads; C3.2 for the gaseous-exchange life process that stops. Distinct from the xylem item above, where the transport mechanism itself was the object.

C5.3 names dance forms and sports explicitly, so a question built on classical and folk dance poses belongs to C-5.3-LO-2; LO-1 covers naming the joint types. Not C6.1 - the Indian dance is the setting, not a claim about the contribution of India to science.
Pure structure-to-function: which cellular features (thin wall, dense cytoplasm, large nucleus) permit repeated division. No differentiation from permanent tissue is required, so LO-1 is not cited.

Identifies the malfunctioning tissue from a lost function, which is the role-of-tissues outcome; LO-1 second because the distractor set forces a xylem-vs-phloem discrimination. Not C3.2 - food translocation is not one of the transport processes that competency lists.
Thinness of the epithelium is asked to be justified by diffusion distance - structure related to function. C3.2 second for the exchange-of-materials process being served.

Two jumps compared for joint behaviour under load: the correlation between tissues and physical fitness, which is what C-5.3-LO-2 asks for. Not LO-1 - no joint is being classified here, the same joints are compared across two conditions.
Straight classification against a closed list of joint types, which is the last clause of LO-1. No fitness or movement-quality reasoning is demanded, so C-5.3-LO-2 is not cited.

Every assertion-reason pair turns on whether a stated structure explains a stated function (flat single-layer epithelium, mitochondria in cardiac muscle, tendon attachment), so C-4.2-LO-2 leads; LO-1 covers the cardiac-muscle and tendon/ligament discriminations the distractors rest on.

The task is literally plot-a-graph-from-a-table then read a trend off it: C-8.2-LO-2. C-8.2-LO-3 for the analysis of the growth pattern in scientific terms. The annual-ring content is the vehicle; the assessed skill is data handling.

Parts (i)-(iii) are consequences of losing bark, phloem and cambium - roles of tissues in a plant. Part (iv) asks the student to surface and vary their own assumptions, which only the C8.2 inquiry competency covers; no LO under C8.2 mentions assumptions.

Collenchyma/sclerenchyma family, split by what the question asks: here the payoff is what the flexibility does for a sapling in monsoon wind, so role (C-4.2-LO-3) joins structure-to-function. Contrast 080b7aa0, where the work was telling the two tissues apart (LO-1).

Three of four parts are experimental design - what differed, what was measured, what must be held constant for a fair comparison - which is the C8.2 competency (identifies variables). Not LO-6: that outcome is specific to apical meristem, and this cutting experiment turns on intercalary meristem, covered by C-4.2-LO-3.

The whole exchange is about whether the simple-tissue definition survives contact with complex tissues, i.e. the simple/complex discrimination named in LO-1. C-4.2-LO-4 rejected: no organ or organism level is invoked.
Asks which structural features produce the toughness and why parenchyma cannot, so structure-to-function leads; LO-1 second for the sclerenchyma-vs-parenchyma contrast the second half forces.

Corrects a claim about where meristematic tissue is found (apical only vs lateral and intercalary too), sitting under the meristematic/permanent discrimination of LO-1. C8.2 for the second half, which asks the student to frame a probing question rather than give an answer.

Weak fit, recorded as such: the content is cell-level (vacuole size), below anything the tissue outcomes cover. LO-1 cited only as the nearest plant-vs-animal discrimination; C8.2 for part (ii), which asks for the assumptions behind the answer.

Tests a one-tissue-one-function claim against the variants of parenchyma (chlorenchyma, aerenchyma) - the role of various tissues. C8.2 because the student is asked what questions to pose and which cases to examine, i.e. to design the check rather than report the answer.
Asks for the definition of a tissue within the cell-tissue-organ-organism hierarchy of a multicellular body, which is precisely C-4.2-LO-4. Not LO-1 - no two tissues are being compared.

The answer turns on why plant and animal tissues differ at all (mobility vs fixed support), the first discrimination listed in LO-1. No single tissue structure or role is at issue, so neither C-4.2-LO-2 nor C-4.2-LO-3 is cited.

Identification is made through the role - producing new branches or leaves at a node points to intercalary meristem. LO-1 withheld by rule: every option is a meristem subtype, and apical/lateral/intercalary is not one of the discriminations LO-1 lists.

The distractor set is meristematic vs simple permanent vs complex permanent vs epidermal, so the assessed act is the meristematic/permanent discrimination in LO-1. Split from 79e9afa3, which needed the meristem subtype rather than the meristem/permanent line.

LO-6 names this experiment exactly: growth in a plant due to apical meristem, here by cutting onion root tips and measuring afterwards. C8.2 for the procedural-sequencing skill the item actually scores.
